Article Title: Meet Washington state student Siddhi Tandon, who did not know where to deposit her first paycheck and created a financial-literacy initiative that has reached over 22,000 people, expanding into six st

Siddhi TandonPhoto credit: Cubs of Wall Street

The paycheck that changed everything

Teaching herself first

Building Cubs of Wall Street

Meeting young people where they are

A book that extends the mission

Why the gap matters

The road ahead

Siddhi Tandon was 15 when she earned her first paycheck, about $500 from working as a camp counselor. She went to the bank to deposit it, only to learn that she could not use the account she already had under her parents’ names. That moment of confusion became the starting point for Cubs of Wall Street, a youth-led financial literacy nonprofit that has now reached more than 22,000 people and expanded into six states, according to Points of Light and Northwest Asian Weekly.Tandon’s story is not just about learning how to manage money. It is about recognising a gap, filling it with practical knowledge, and then inviting other young people to do the same. Her initiative now includes free workshops, a published book, trained chapter leaders, and partnerships with libraries and credit unions across Washington and beyond. Read more about her initiatives, as per the reports, here:Tandon, a student at Lakeside School in Seattle, opened her first paycheck during the summer before her sophomore year. She had earned the money as a camp counselor, but when she tried to deposit it, the bank teller told her she could not use the account under her parents’ names.Instead, she opened a teen checking account. That experience made her realise how little she knew about what she could actually do with money once she earned it.“This is the first time it struck me because it was the first time I’d really had money in my life,” she told Northwest Asian Weekly.That realisation pushed her to start learning about personal finance on her own.Throughout her sophomore year, Tandon taught herself about personal finance and the stock market using YouTube videos, online articles, and conversations with her parents. By the end of that school year, she had opened a custodial investment account, as per the reports.Rather than keeping that knowledge to herself, she decided to share it. She spoke at TEDxDelMar Youth in San Diego, delivering a talk titled 'The Cubs of Capital Street: Smart Money Starts Young'.At the time, she was only 16 and worried whether people would take her seriously. The response was immediate. Adults told her they wished someone had shared this information with them when they were younger, and children said they were inspired to open bank accounts.By August 2025, Tandon had founded Cubs of Wall Street, a youth-led financial literacy initiative. The organisation began by hosting free workshops in public libraries across Washington, covering budgeting, saving, investing, and different types of accounts, including cryptocurrency.By early 2026, the initiative had reached more than 4,500 students through library sessions, school STEAM nights, and community events from the Eastside to Federal Way. One of the early sessions at the Redmond Library drew around 70 people, a turnout that surprised and encouraged Tandon.The organisation has since grown into a network spanning six states and an international chapter. Tandon has personally taught more than 250 students and families, while the broader programming has reached more than 22,000 community members.Tandon’s teaching style is interactive rather than lecture-based. She reads the room, adapts to what participants already know, and uses games and real-life examples to make financial concepts easier to understand.One of her most popular exercises involves compound interest. She asks participants whether they would rather have $50,000 at the end of a month or a penny that doubles every day for 30 days. Most choose the $50,000, only to learn that the doubling penny grows to more than $5 million by the end of the month.That kind of hands-on approach has helped her connect with audiences of different backgrounds. At some libraries, students cite research papers, while at others, they have never heard of a bank account. Tandon sees those differences as proof that financial education is needed everywhere.In February 2026, Tandon published her first book, What I Learned About Money: A High Schooler’s Account. The nonfiction book is aimed at readers ages 9 to 18 and covers earning, budgeting, saving, investing, and taxes.Each section ends with a chapter about a well-known figure, from Warren Buffett to Oprah Winfrey, who has used those financial skills in real life. The book is available through the Seattle Public Library, the King County Library System, and Amazon.Tandon said the idea for the book came directly from her workshops. People often asked for the slides she used, which made her realise that a book could help spread the knowledge even further.Washington is one of 11 states without mandated financial literacy education in high school, according to Points of Light. That gap is what Tandon is trying to close through her nonprofit and her advocacy.Research by Tyton Partners in collaboration with Next Gen Personal Finance found that completing just one semester of personal finance in high school can translate into an average lifetime economic benefit of about $100,000 per student. Tandon cited that figure in her TEDx talk and has made it central to her push for systemic change.Her goal is to see a semester or workshop of mandatory financial literacy education implemented in high schools. She believes financial education influences nearly every major decision people make in adult life, from managing income and credit to securing housing and planning for the future.Tandon is now recruiting peers in other states to open Cubs of Wall Street chapters, expanding the organisation’s reach. Her hope is that more young people will see financial literacy as something they can engage with early, rather than something they have to figure out later.“I’m not too young to think about this. I’m not too young to care about this,” she said, as per Northwest Asian Weekly. That message is at the heart of everything she has built.For a student who once did not know where to deposit a paycheck, Tandon has come a long way. Her initiative is now helping thousands of others avoid the same confusion and take their first steps toward financial confidence.

Article Title: 'Addressing existing threats': Yemeni forces withdraw from Bab el-Mandeb as Houthis cement foothold
Article Text:
The Houthis have continued attacks on Saudi Arabia, a key US ally and the world's largest crude oil exporter (Photo: Reuters).

Military campaign and Houthi advances

Saudi backed Yemeni forces said on Sunday they were withdrawing from an area overlooking the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait, leaving Iran-aligned Houthi rebels in control of the territory.The southern Yemeni forces said they were redeploying towards Aden, where the internationally recognised government is based, Reuters reported."The Southern Armed Forces announce the implementation of a redeployment operation for its forces from Dhubab Airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area, west of Taiz Governorate," the southern forces said in a statement."This step is taken based on the priority of securing the capital, Aden, and the neighbouring governorates, as well as strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats."The move comes as the Houthis, who control much of northern Yemen, including the capital Sanaa and the country's most populous areas, step up pressure on southern territories still held by government forces.The withdrawal could give the Houthis greater leverage over one of the world's most important maritime chokepoints, potentially increasing pressure on global shipping at a time when Iran continues to disrupt traffic through the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula.Simultaneous pressure on the two waterways could further restrict Gulf oil producers' access to their main shipping routes, Reuters reported.The Bab el-Mandeb Strait is a major route for global shipments of commodities and other goods, particularly cargo travelling from Asia to Europe through Egypt's Suez Canal.In October, the Government forces launched a military campaign to recapture strategic coastal areas from the Houthis, who had advanced south in September in an attempt to take control of Yemen's entire Red Sea coastline. The rapid offensive brought the group within reach of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.The latest escalation has opened another volatile front in the wider US-Israeli war on Iran. The fighting also broke a United Nations-brokered truce that had been in place since 2022.The Houthis have continued attacks on Saudi Arabia , a key US ally and the world's largest crude oil exporter.The kingdom had experienced relative calm during the early months of the nine-month-old Iran war, but recent Houthi strikes have disrupted flights and oil supplies.The group has targeted Saudi ports, airports and facilities belonging to state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco, including Yanbu, the kingdom's oil export hub on the Red Sea.Saudi Arabia has responded by striking Houthi targets in Yemen, which has been embroiled in civil war since 2014, when the group pushed the government out of the capital and towards the south.
Article Summary: Yemeni forces withdraw from area overlooking strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Move leaves Iran-aligned Houthi rebels in control of the territory. Move comes as Houthis step up pressure on southern territories still held by government. withdrawal could give Houthis greater leverage over one of world's most important maritime chokepoints.

Article Text:

Jordan has sentenced three men to death for their involvement in a terrorist attack on a Greek Orthodox church in the southern Karak Governorate last month that killed nine people.The state security court handed down the sentences on Sunday after convicting the three of several terrorism-related offences, including carrying out attacks that resulted in deaths, using weapons and ammunition for terrorist purposes, possessing weapons with terrorist intent, conspiring to carry out armed attacks and promoting the ideology of a terrorist group, as per state-owned news agency Petro.One of the three was also found guilty of providing funds to finance terrorist acts under Jordan's Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Law No. 20 of 2021.The verdict is subject to automatic appeal before the court of cassation under Jordanian law.The attack took place on October 23 at St George’s Greek Orthodox Church in the village of Hammoud, in Karak Governorate, during a funeral procession. It left nine people dead and several others injured.Following the attack, security forces launched extensive searches and investigations to identify those responsible. On October 26, the Public Security Directorate announced that the three primary suspects had been arrested at an abandoned house in Karak.According to the security authorities, the suspects refused to surrender and engaged security forces before they were apprehended.
Article Summary: Jordan sentences three men to death for their involvement in a terrorist attack on a Greek Orthodox church last month. The attack took place on October 23 at St George’s Greek Orthodox Church in the village of Hammoud, in Karak Governorate, during a funeral procession. One of the three was also found guilty of providing funds to finance terrorist acts.

Article Title: A London mother who died at 94 left her entire £1.1 million estate to her eldest son after accusing her daughter of not showing enough love and respect, and a judge has now rejected the daughter’s cha
Article Text:
Representative Image (AI Generated)

Daughter alleged brother influenced mother's decision

Judge finds no evidence of undue influence

A family dispute over a £1.1 million inheritance has ended with a UK judge upholding the will of a London mother who excluded her daughter and younger son from her estate, saying they had failed to show her enough “love and respect”. According to a report by The Independent, Dervishe Halil, who died aged 94 in 2021, left her entire estate to her eldest son, Dogan Halil, in her final will, drawn up in 2018. Her daughter, Aysel Gencay, challenged the document, alleging that her brother had manipulated their mother into changing her inheritance plans. The court rejected her claims and ruled that the will was valid.Dervishe, who was originally from Cyprus, moved to London with her husband in 1952. She had three children and, in earlier versions of her will, intended to divide her wealth among them. However, relations within the family deteriorated following a dispute between Dogan and his younger sister Aysel. The disagreement centred partly on a valuable family property in Packington Street, Islington, with Aysel accusing her brother of taking part of the property for his own benefit.The family tensions eventually affected Dervishe's estate plans.Between 2013 and 2018, she made four wills, changing how her assets would be distributed. In 2015, she sent a handwritten letter to Aysel and her younger son, Attila, warning that they risked being excluded from her will unless they reconciled with Dogan and treated him and their mother with greater respect.In the letter, Dervishe criticised their behaviour towards their eldest brother, writing: “Your actions have destroyed my life and home, your actions towards your brother Dogan are very bad and shameful, we saw nothing but goodness from Dogan to all of us”. Three years later, she acted on the warning. Her 2018 will left the entire estate to Dogan, excluding Aysel and Attila. A separate handwritten note explained the decision, saying the conditions set out in her earlier letter had not been fulfilled.“You still do not talk to your brother Dogan, and you still do not show me love and respect. You destroyed my home and I deleted you from my will,” she wrote, according to the court reporting.Dervishe died in 2021, leaving an estate valued at approximately £1.1 million. Aysel subsequently brought a legal challenge against Dogan, who was administering the estate, arguing that their mother would not have independently decided to disinherit her.Aysel argued that Dogan had exerted undue influence over their mother and turned her against the younger siblings. Her legal team questioned whether Dervishe had understood and approved the contents of her final will, or whether she had been pressured into signing it. Her barrister, Peter John, argued that the decision was inconsistent with what Aysel understood to be her mother's longstanding approach to inheritance: treating her children equally. He also questioned the authenticity and authorship of the handwritten letters, arguing that Dervishe could not have composed them without significant assistance. The language used in the letters, he suggested, bore similarities to Dogan's correspondence.Aysel, who lived in Turkey, told the court that she had remained close to her mother and regularly travelled from Istanbul to visit her during her later years. “I remained extremely close to my mother all my life,” she said. She also maintained that her brother had influenced Dervishe's views and that the final will did not reflect their mother's genuine wishes. Her case included allegations of fraudulent calumny, a legal claim involving false statements that allegedly cause someone to change their will.Dogan denied the allegations. His position was that his mother had made her own decision and that he had not been involved in preparing the will or the accompanying letters. His wife, Susan, was also involved in the proceedings as a co-executor. Attila was a co-defendant, although Dogan and Susan had subsequently arranged for him to receive a one-third share of the estate through a deed of variation.Judge Mark Raeside KC, hearing the dispute at Central London County Court, rejected Aysel's allegations and upheld the 2018 will. He found that Dogan had not helped prepare the document or the handwritten letters explaining his mother's decision. “I reject the assertion that the deceased had any assistance from Dogan with her will. The evidence makes clear he was simply a dutiful son,” the judge said. He added that both side letters had been written in Turkish in Dervishe's own handwriting and that Dogan had nothing to do with them.The court also considered evidence from the solicitor who prepared the will. Dervishe had attended the solicitor's office on her own, and the solicitor's records indicated that she appeared mentally sharp and understood what she was doing. When asked why she wanted to exclude her other children, she reportedly explained that they were not visiting her or showing interest in her.Aysel had also questioned whether her mother possessed the mental capacity to make the will. However, the judge rejected this argument, noting that although Dervishe displayed symptoms of dementia by 2020, that did not establish that she lacked the capacity to make decisions in 2018, when the contested will was drawn up. The judge also dismissed the allegations of dishonesty against Dogan, describing Aysel as having become “fixated” on trying to prove her brother had acted improperly. He said there was no dishonesty by Dogan and dismissed the case.
Article Summary: Dervishe Halil left her entire estate to her eldest son, Dogan Halil, in her final will, drawn up in 2018. Her daughter, Aysel Gencay, challenged the document, alleging that her brother had manipulated their mother into changing her inheritance plans. The court rejected her claims and ruled that the will was valid.

Article Title: An Iranian shipping businessman left his $3.2 million in US assets to the eldest of his three daughters, a jury sided with her, and now a Maryland appeals court has ordered a new hearing for her two s
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

An inheritance dispute over nearly $3.2 million in US assets left by an Iranian shipping businessman has returned to court after a Maryland appeals court overturned a jury's decision in favour of his eldest daughter. The case centres on whether Seyedkazem Amini-Nejad, who died in 2023 at the age of 95, understood the estate documents that left his American assets exclusively to one of his three daughters. In a ruling dated October 28, 2026, the Appellate Court of Maryland said the jury had been given an incorrect legal standard when considering the younger daughters' claim that their sister deliberately interfered with their expected inheritance.Amini-Nejad had spent most of his life in Iran, where he co-owned a shipping company with two business partners. He travelled to the United States to visit his family and receive medical treatment. All three of his daughters lived in the US, and the eldest, Ellahe Amini-Nejad, had been involved in managing his finances and accompanying him to medical and legal appointments during his visits.The dispute arose from estate-planning documents signed during a visit to the US in March 2019.On March 22 that year, Amini-Nejad signed a will stating that his cash, liquid assets, stocks, shares, bank accounts, life insurance policies and retirement benefits should go to Ellahe. She was also named the executor and personal representative of the will. A trust was established soon afterwards, with Ellahe named as its sole trustee and beneficiary. Court records show that $3,199,794 was transferred into the trust. The documents did not name his younger daughters, Elham and Eman, as beneficiaries.The arrangements became contentious after Amini-Nejad died on May 23, 2023. The younger sisters said they had not been informed about the will or trust and discovered the documents only after travelling to Iran for their father's funeral. While searching through his belongings at the family home in Tehran, they found a folder containing estate papers, bank documents and handwritten notes in Farsi.The notes became an important part of their challenge. Elham testified that she was certain the handwriting on a note attached to the will belonged to her eldest sister. The younger daughters argued that their father spoke limited English and could not have adequately understood the English-language legal documents he had signed. They also maintained that he had wanted his three daughters to remain united and share his estate.The sisters filed a lawsuit in Maryland in January 2024, alleging fraud, undue influence, intentional interference with their expected inheritance and financial exploitation. They sought to have the trust invalidated and compensation for the assets they believed had been wrongfully diverted.During the trial, the eldest daughter disputed the allegations and maintained that her father had independently chosen how to distribute his American assets. The attorney who prepared the estate documents testified that he communicated with Amini-Nejad in both Farsi and English and believed his client understood the arrangements and was acting voluntarily. The court also heard that all three daughters had accompanied their father to appointments during his visits to the US.The younger sisters pointed to another decision their father had made: in August 2021, he transferred the deed of the family home in Tehran to all three daughters. They argued that this was consistent with his wish to treat them equally. They also questioned why the will and trust had not been disclosed to them while their father was alive.After a four-day trial in Howard County Circuit Court, the jury found that Elham and Eman had a reasonable expectation of receiving an inheritance. However, it ruled in favour of Ellahe on their claim of intentional interference, finding that they had not established that she had engaged in wrongful conduct with the purpose of preventing them from receiving the inheritance. The crucial issue was the standard of proof the jury had been instructed to apply. The trial judge had told jurors that the younger sisters needed to establish their claim through "clear and convincing evidence", a relatively demanding standard used in certain civil cases, including fraud claims.The sisters challenged that instruction on appeal, arguing that the court should instead have applied the lower standard of "preponderance of the evidence". Under this standard, a claim is established when the evidence makes it more likely than not that the alleged conduct occurred. The Appellate Court of Maryland agreed. In its October 28 opinion, written by Judge Kathryn Graeff, the court said the correct standard for intentional interference with an expected inheritance was preponderance of the evidence. It reasoned that the claim was closely related to other civil claims involving interference with economic interests, for which the lower standard applies.The court also referred to the legal framework adopted when Maryland first recognised intentional interference with an inheritance as a civil claim in 2020. That earlier decision had not specified the burden of proof. The appeals court said the standard should be consistent with the principles governing interference with economic expectations.It further explained that the incorrect instruction could have affected the jury's decision. Since jurors had been asked to apply a higher standard than the law required, the appeals court said it could not determine whether they might have reached a different conclusion under the correct test. It therefore reversed the judgment and sent the case back for further proceedings.The ruling does not establish that Ellahe committed fraud, manipulated her father or unlawfully took the money. Nor does it automatically award any portion of the trust to the younger sisters. Instead, it gives them another opportunity to pursue their inheritance-interference claim under the correct legal standard. The court did not need to decide other issues raised in the appeal, including disputes concerning expert handwriting evidence and testimony from the lawyer who drafted the trust.The case also highlights a legal distinction between challenging the validity of estate documents and claiming that someone deliberately interfered with an expected inheritance. While the younger sisters raised allegations of fraud and undue influence, the appellate decision focused on the standard of proof applicable to the interference claim. The next proceedings will determine whether the younger daughters can establish their allegations under the standard clarified by the appeals court.
Article Summary: The case centres on whether Seyedkazem Amini-Nejad understood the estate documents that left his American assets exclusively to one of his three daughters. The Appellate Court of Maryland said the jury had been given an incorrect legal standard when considering the younger daughters' claim that their sister deliberately interfered with their expected inheritance.

The controversy has raised questions about potential security risks involving the world's leading artificial intelligence chipmaker.

Article Text:
Chuck Schumer (left) faces first leadership challenge in decades as Van Hollen enters race

Van Hollen gets support from Sanders, El-Sayed

Disagreement over Schumer's leadership

Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland has announced a bid to become the next Senate Majority Leader, challenging incumbent Democratic leader Chuck Schumer after the party's victories in the US midterm elections.Van Hollen said on Thursday that he was running because “the American people called for change” and argued that Democrats needed new leadership to respond to the election result.“It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership,” Van Hollen said in a statement. “This is not about any one person — it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader.”The leadership election will be held by secret ballot in early December. It is expected to be the first contested election for the position of Democratic leader in decades, with senators privately debating whether Schumer should continue in the role.Schumer has said he has enough support to retain the position. In a statement following Van Hollen’s announcement, he welcomed discussions about the future of the caucus and reiterated that he had the votes to remain its leader.“I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together — 55 seats and counting is an amazing result — and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader,” Schumer said. “I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people.”Schumer has been speaking to Democratic senators since the election and working on the party's agenda for 2027. During private caucus meetings this week, he outlined a broad plan for the first 100 days of the new majority.“I’m going to win it,” Schumer told the news agency Associated Press in an interview last week.Van Hollen has received endorsements from independent Senator Bernie Sanders , who caucuses with Democrats, and Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan.Sanders said the election result reflected a demand for a Democratic Party that would challenge powerful special interests and the billionaire class while fighting for working families.“The American people voted for change. They want a Democratic Party that will stand up to powerful special interests, take on the billionaire class and fight for working families. That is why I am supporting Senator Chris Van Hollen to lead Senate Democrats,” Sanders said.El-Sayed had also backed Van Hollen's leadership bid, saying the party needed “bold leadership” after the election.“I called on Sen. @ChrisVanHollen to lead our caucus as a candidate back in April because he leads with courage and experience,” El-Sayed wrote on X. “We need both right now. Which is why I’m proud to stand with him in his bid to lead our Senate majority.”Sanders and Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan had called for new leadership at a press conference on Tuesday, although neither had then endorsed a specific candidate, AP reported.Several Democratic senators have publicly backed Schumer, including incoming Ohio Senator Sherrod Brown, who defeated Republican Senator Jon Husted in last week's election.Maine Senator Angus King, an independent who caucuses with Democrats and votes in the leadership election, also defended Schumer after Van Hollen's announcement.“Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?” King said, adding that Schumer was “one of the principal architects of the most successful election in modern history”.The contest follows divisions within the Democratic caucus that became more visible in spring 2025, when Schumer faced criticism after siding with Republicans on a spending vote.Although he subsequently led Democrats through a government shutdown and helped the party's candidates during the midterm campaign, sections of the party's base have continued to call for generational change.Van Hollen, 67, is 75-year-old Schumer's challenger. He has presented himself as a new face for the party and has also said he is considering a presidential run.Speaking to MS NOW, Van Hollen said his decision to contest the leadership position was driven by what he described as a broader demand for change in Washington.“This is not about any one individual, but it is about answering the call of the American people. We saw a huge outburst of democracy on Election Day — red states, blue states, purple states — and it wasn’t only a rejection of Donald Trump and his corruption and his wars and his cruelty, it was also about a call for a larger change to take on a broken economic system that’s rigged in favor of the very wealthy against working people, led by a corrupt political system,” he said.Van Hollen also criticised Schumer's involvement in Democratic primaries, accusing him of supporting establishment candidates instead of focusing on defeating Republicans.“We shouldn't have a leader who is getting involved in picking sides in open Democratic primaries, and we should be focused on defeating Republicans. We have two senators right now in the Senate who wouldn't be there if the current majority leader had his way.He supported establishment candidates in the primaries,” he told MS NOW.Van Hollen has also called for action against President Donald Trump over allegations of corruption, supported efforts to impeach defence secretary Pete Hegseth and urged Congress to defund the war in Iran.The December ballot will determine who leads the Senate Democratic caucus as it prepares to take control of the chamber in the next Congress.
Article Summary: Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland has announced a bid to become the next Senate Majority Leader. It is expected to be the first contested election for the position of Democratic leader in decades, with senators privately debating whether Schumer should continue in the role. Schumer has said he has enough support to retain the position.

Article Title: Spain Protest: Protesters clash with police, set fires during Spain's general strike: Watch
Article Text:
Protesters set fires, clash with police during Spain's general strike: Watch

Clashes broke out between masked protesters and police in Barcelona on Wednesday as tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike in 14 years, called by the country's major trade unions over the housing affordability crisis and rising cost of living.Around 120,000 people joined demonstrations in Madrid and more than 50,000 gathered in Barcelona, where some protesters set fire to rubbish bins, smashed shop windows and clashed with police. Officers fired tear gas to disperse the crowds, while transport and other public services across the country faced significant disruption.The disturbances in Barcelona continued into the evening, with a heavy police presence in the city centre. Some clashes took place along Passeig de Gràcia, near the iconic Plaça de Catalunya. Local media reported that protesters fired fireworks at police and looted shops, including a Lego store. Some were also seen attempting to enter an Apple Store.The unions said around four million workers participated in the nationwide strike, which was backed by Spain's two largest labour organisations, the UGT and CCOO, as well as tenants' associations protesting against rising rents and evictions.UGT chief Pepe Álvarez described the strike as a success, citing "massive" participation, while CCOO leader Unai Sordo said turnout was "very significant". However, participation varied across the country, with stronger support in coastal regions where housing pressures have been particularly acute.The walkout was the first general strike in Spain since 2012, when workers protested against austerity measures during the eurozone debt crisis. It comes less than three weeks before parliamentary elections scheduled for November 29.Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is seeking to make housing affordability a central election issue and shift the political debate away from corruption cases involving his inner circle and a deadly train crash last month. His Socialist Party, however, continues to trail in opinion polls.Spain faces a housing deficit of around 750,000 homes, which is projected to exceed one million by 2028, according to the country's central bank.With home ownership becoming increasingly unaffordable, demand for rental accommodation has risen sharply, putting further pressure on the market. The average monthly rent of 1,176 euros ($1,315) is equivalent to about 98.7 per cent of a young person's average monthly salary in Spain, according to the Youth Council of Spain.
Article Summary: Around 120,000 people joined demonstrations in Madrid and more than 50,000 gathered in Barcelona. Some protesters set fire to rubbish bins, smashed shop windows and clashed with police. Article Title: 'I may be jailed, they may try to kill me': Sheikh Hasina's defiant message on returning to Bangladesh
Article Text:
Hasina opens up on fears, threats and Bangladesh return

Denies ordering killings during 2024 uprising

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Rejects International Crimes Tribunal verdict

Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has said that the threat of arrest, imprisonment or even death would not stop her from returning to Dhaka, asserting that she would rather die in her homeland than stay away from her people.In a rare audio interview with news agency IANS, Hasina said she was fully aware of the risks involved in returning to Bangladesh but maintained that fear had never stopped her from doing what she believed was right.“Look, I understand the risks very well. I may be arrested the moment I arrive. They may send me to prison. They may even try to kill me. I have considered all these possibilities. But, you know, I stopped worrying about my personal safety a long time ago. I returned to Bangladesh in 1981, despite military rule. I returned again in 2007, knowing that the military-backed government might arrest me. I have faced imprisonment and repeated attempts on my life. Fear has never stopped me from doing what I believe is right,” the exiled leader stated.Expressing concern over the situation in Bangladesh, Hasina said the country was going through a difficult phase, alleging that Awami League leaders and workers were being persecuted while ordinary people were suffering and losing their homes and livelihoods.She said the hardships faced by the people had strengthened her determination to return and stand by them, irrespective of the consequences.“Today, my country is going through a terrible time. Our leaders and workers are being persecuted. Ordinary people are suffering, and families are losing their homes and livelihoods. How can I stay away while my people face such hardship? I have spent my entire political life with the people of Bangladesh. Whatever happens to me, I want to stand beside them. If I have to die, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina told IANS.Addressing allegations over deaths during the 2024 uprising in Bangladesh, the former prime minister categorically denied ordering the killing of innocent people.Hasina accused the former Muhammad Yunus-led interim government of stopping a judicial inquiry she had initiated into the deaths and subsequently granting legal protection to participants in the uprising for acts classified as “political resistance”.“Let me make one thing very clear. I never ordered the killing of innocent people. I reject that accusation completely. Every death was tragic. As Prime Minister, I had a responsibility to protect the lives of our citizens, and I wanted to know exactly what had happened. That is why, on July 18, 2024, I established a Judicial Enquiry Commission headed by a High Court judge. On August 1, I expanded it to a three-member commission so that every incident could be examined properly. But what happened after Muhammad Yunus assumed power? He stopped that investigation,” the former PM said.She questioned the interim administration's decision to halt the inquiry while pursuing murder cases against her and thousands of Awami League leaders, activists and workers.“His administration subsequently granted legal protection to participants in the uprising for acts classified as political resistance. At the same time, murder cases were brought against me and thousands of Awami League leaders, activists and workers. If they really wanted the truth, why did they stop the judicial investigation that I had already established? Why should there be different standards of justice depending on someone's political identity?” she questioned.Hasina also rejected the proceedings of Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) and the verdict against her, alleging that she was not given a genuine opportunity to defend herself.“As for the tribunal, I reject both the proceedings and the verdict. I was denied what I consider a genuine opportunity to defend myself. I will examine whatever lawful options are available to challenge that verdict,” she told IANS.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina says she would rather die in her homeland than stay away from her people. Denies ordering killings during 2024 uprising in Bangladesh. Rejects International Crimes Tribunal verdict against her. Says she was not given a genuine opportunity to defend herself.

Article Title: 10 killed as passenger vehicle plunges 500 metres down slope in Nepal
Article Text:
10 killed in passenger vehicle accident in Nepal (File photo)

At least 10 people were killed and five others injured on Thursday after a passenger vehicle plunged down a steep slope in Nepal's Makawanpur district in Bagmati province, according to media reports.The accident took place at around 5:45am when the vehicle, carrying around 15 people, was travelling from Kathmandu to Sarlahi, a local newspaper reported.The vehicle reportedly plunged around 500 metres down a steep slope, killing 10 people and injuring five others.The deceased included three women, two girls and five men, the report said, adding that their identities were yet to be established.The injured were taken to Hetauda Hospital for treatment, The Kathmandu Post reported.A seven-member rescue team was deployed to the accident site following reports of the crash, it added.
Article Summary: Vehicle plunged down a steep slope in Nepal's Makawanpur district. Accident took place at around 5:45am when the vehicle was travelling from Kathmandu to Sarlahi. The deceased included three women, two girls and five men, according to reports.

Article Title: 'Somebody hit us': Audio captures moment jets collided at Miami airport
Article Text:
Two planes collide at Miami airport

Airlines cooperate with FAA investigation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Collision follows nationwide US flight disruption

NEW DELHI: "Somebody hit us," a Copa Airlines pilot told air traffic controllers moments after a UPS cargo aircraft struck the passenger jet on the taxiway at Miami International Airport, as audio recordings of the incident shed light on the sequence of events leading to the collision.The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has launched an investigation into the incident, which involved a UPS Boeing 767 and a Copa Airlines Boeing 737. Two people sustained minor injuries, according to the information provided.The Copa Airlines flight had arrived from Panama City with 166 passengers and six crew members on board and was taxiing towards the terminal. The UPS aircraft was preparing to depart for Bogota, Colombia.According to air traffic control (ATC) audio, controllers had instructed the UPS crew to give way to the arriving Copa aircraft before the two planes made contact."Somebody hit us," the Copa pilot told the control tower after the collision.The controller then questioned the UPS crew about whether its aircraft had struck the passenger jet."Yeah, we went too far, and then he clipped us with the wing," the UPS pilot replied.The Copa pilot subsequently reported damage to the aircraft, saying: "It seems that we are missing the left wingtip."Both airlines have said they will cooperate with the FAA investigation.Copa Airlines said it regretted the disruption caused to passengers and reiterated that their safety remained its priority.The airline said all 172 people on board were safely disembarked after the aircraft was towed to the gate.UPS also confirmed that its crew members were unharmed and said it was committed to assisting authorities in determining the cause of the collision.The preliminary information and ATC recording point to a possible failure to follow ground movement instructions. The FAA investigation will establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.The incident occurred less than 24 hours after a nationwide FAA ground stop on Friday disrupted air travel across the United States.The ground stop triggered thousands of flight cancellations and delays, leaving passengers stranded at airports and forcing many to wait for rebooked flights.The latest collision has added to concerns over aviation operations in the US following a weekend of widespread travel disruption.
Article Summary: Collision follows nationwide US flight disruption on Friday. US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has launched an investigation into the incident. Two people sustained minor injuries, according to the information provided. Both airlines have said they will cooperate with the FAA investigation.

Article Title: An American family has five generations born on September 14; a baby boy born in 2025 helped them set a Guinness World Record spanning 118 years
Article Text:
​Donald Harlow, Arthur Bell and Emma Bell Image Courtesy: Guinness World Record

Five generations , one birthday and a rather impressive family tradition

A birthday party that requires a family tree

When coincidence starts looking suspiciously like fate

A record that takes a village (and several generations)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Imagine being born into a family where your great-great-grandfather, great-grandmother, grandfather, mother and you all share the same birthday. Suddenly, arriving fashionably late is not an option. Neither is being born on September 15.For one American family, September 14 is not just another date on the calendar. It is practically a family heirloom. And with the arrival of a baby boy in 2025, the Bell and Harlow family has managed to turn a rather unusual birthday coincidence into a Guinness World Record . The pressure to perform must have been tremendous.The story began in 1907, when Wilber Harlow was born on September 14. A postmaster who also owned the Harlow General Store in Brooks, Iowa, Wilber probably had no idea that his birthday would go on to become something of a family institution.42 years later, on September 14, 1949, Wilber and his wife welcomed their daughter, Addie Harlow. Two generations down, and the family was already sharing a surname and a birthday.The coincidence continued in 1972, when Addie gave birth to her son, Donald Harlow, on September 14. Donald, in turn, welcomed his daughter Emma in 1997, also on September 14.At this point, one might reasonably suspect that September 14 had been reserved exclusively for the Harlow family.But the universe was not quite finished with its little joke. In 2025, Emma and her husband Wyatt welcomed their son Arthur Bell. His due date? September 14. And, as if the family had not already made its point, Arthur arrived on the very same day as his mother, grandfather, great-grandmother and great-great-grandfather.That makes five generations born on the same calendar date, spanning 118 years. The achievement earned the American family the Guinness World Records title for the most generations born on the same day in recorded human history.Most families struggle to organise one birthday party without somebody forgetting to order the cake. The Bells and Harlows, meanwhile, have managed to combine five generations into one annual celebration. Imagine the sugar levels on that day.According to Guinness World Records, the family had been aware of its unusual streak for years. With four generations already sharing September 14, they knew they had something special. However, they held off on applying for the record because they had a rather ambitious idea: they wanted to see whether a fifth generation could join the club.When Emma discovered that her second child's due date could fall on the family birthday, the possibility suddenly became much more real. And when Arthur arrived on September 14, the family finally had its five-generation record."We kind of always knew that we held a record with four generations, we just never applied because we had that ambition to have the fifth on 14 September," Emma told Guinness World Records.Well, talk about setting the bar high for your children. Most parents are happy if their offspring remember to call on their birthday. The Harlows appear to have made the actual date of birth a family expectation.There is another curious detail to the story. The five birthdays also follow an alternating pattern of genders: boy, girl, boy, girl, boy. Wilber, Addie, Donald, Emma and Arthur have managed to keep the sequence going for more than a century.Sadly, Addie passed away in 2023 and never got to meet her great-grandson Arthur. However, she was part of the family's birthday celebrations for years. The gatherings usually involved heading to a restaurant and sharing a cake with candles, which must have required increasingly careful counting.Of course, the internet had a few questions when the record came to light. And some were rather less sentimental than others.On Reddit, where the story attracted plenty of attention, users wondered whether the family had somehow managed to coordinate five births. Others joked about the pressure on successive generations to ensure that the next baby arrived on the correct date. One commenter even imagined the delivery room as a particularly tense countdown, with everyone waiting for the right moment.To be fair, it is an understandable question. Babies do not generally consult family calendars before deciding to make an entrance. Pregnancy due dates are estimates, and births can happen days or even weeks before or after them.Medical interventions can also make the timing of a delivery more predictable in some circumstances, but that does not mean the family necessarily planned every birth around September 14. Guinness records the coincidence, not a century-long exercise in scheduling pregnancies.Emma's grandfather, Donald, seemed to have a simpler explanation. "God works in beautiful ways," he said.And apparently, God has a rather strong preference for September birthdays.There is one more coincidence that makes the story even more unusual. Wilber and his wife Addie were married in Maryville, Missouri, the same place where Emma and Wyatt eventually met. It is a small detail, perhaps, but one that gives the family history an almost cinematic quality. The same date keeps coming around, and apparently, so does the same location.Before the Bells and Harlows claimed the title, four generations sharing a birthday was already a recognised record. In fact, Guinness notes that the four-generation achievement had been held simultaneously by seven different families, with examples dating back to the 1800s. The fifth generation, however, gave the Harlows the distinction of becoming the sole record holders.This is not a record that can be achieved by one particularly talented individual, a gruelling training regime or an extraordinary display of endurance. It takes generations, a little luck and a coincidence that refuses to let go.Arthur is still very young, so he has plenty of time before he has to worry about breaking any records of his own. But he has already inherited a rather unusual family legacy. Somewhere down the line, he might even find himself explaining to his children why September 14 is a date that absolutely cannot be overlooked.Until then, the family has 118 years of birthdays to celebrate, one Guinness certificate to show for it, and a very good reason to order an exceptionally large cake every September. One can only hope the next generation is not already feeling the pressure.
Article Summary: The Bell and Harlow family has managed to turn a rather unusual birthday coincidence into a Guinness World Record. With the arrival of a baby boy in 2025, the family finally had its five-generation record. Wilber, Addie, Donald, Emma and Arthur have managed to keep the sequence going for more than a century.

Article Text:
Image: Canva

Florida woman allegedly targeted Pokémon cards after argument with ex-boyfriend

She allegedly returned to the apartment and tried to reach the cards again

Police say Pokémon cards were used to provoke her ex-boyfriend

A Florida woman allegedly grabbed her ex-boyfriend’s Pokémon cards during a physical confrontation after realising that the collection was upsetting him, according to police. Nadia Hussain, 23, was arrested in Orlando on November 7 following a dispute at her ex-boyfriend’s apartment. Police said the argument began after he asked her to leave and later escalated into an alleged physical altercation. Hussain is facing charges of domestic battery and witness tampering. The Pokémon cards were not the subject of a theft charge, and police said the collection was not damaged.According to an arrest affidavit cited by Law&Crime, Hussain had spent the night at her ex-boyfriend’s apartment before the two began arguing. He asked her to leave, but she allegedly refused. When he started recording the confrontation and threatened to contact building security, Hussain allegedly knocked his phone from his hand and struck him several times.The argument then turned towards his Pokémon cards, which were lying on a table in the living room. Police said Hussain approached the cards while her ex-boyfriend tried to stop her. She allegedly grabbed them after noticing that doing so affected his behaviour.The situation did not end when Hussain initially left the apartment. The Marry Sue reported that she later returned to collect personal belongings, including a bong she had left behind. Her ex-boyfriend allegedly opened the door slightly to hand it to her after she said she would not come inside.According to the police account, Hussain then allegedly forced her way into the apartment and moved towards the living room. Her ex-boyfriend believed she was trying to get to his Pokémon cards again and blocked her path. The two became involved in another physical confrontation, according to the affidavit.During an interview with police, Hussain allegedly said she had been deliberately annoying her ex-boyfriend because she felt he was not showing her enough affection. She also reportedly acknowledged grabbing the Pokémon cards after seeing how much the action affected him.The confrontation became more serious when her ex-boyfriend tried to call 911. Police said Hussain struck his phone several times in an attempt to stop him from making the call. A 911 hang-up was received from his number, and neighbours eventually intervened to help remove Hussain from the apartment.Hussain was arrested and charged with domestic battery and felony witness tampering for allegedly hindering communication with law enforcement, according to Law&Crime. The reports do not indicate that the Pokémon cards were stolen or damaged. The allegations have not been proven in court.
Article Summary: Florida woman allegedly targeted Pokémon cards after argument with ex-boyfriend. Nadia Hussain, 23, was arrested in Orlando on November 7 following a dispute. Police said the argument began after he asked her to leave and escalated into an alleged physical altercation. Hussain is facing charges of domestic battery and witness tampering.

When a parent dies without leaving a will, disputes among family members can become complicated, particularly when an estate includes property in different states. In Indiana, two half-siblings became involved in a prolonged legal battle over their late father's estate, including real estate in Indiana and California. Although they eventually reached a mediated settlement, disagreements over its terms led to further court proceedings and a substantial financial penalty for the brother.In a November 13, 2026 opinion , the Indiana Court of Appeals upheld sanctions of $177,852.86 against Michael W Clark. The ruling in Michael Clark v. Clark, who died without a will on September 8, 2021. Mrozinski had previously served as her father's power of attorney and was appointed personal representative of his estate after his death.Clark filed a legal action in September 2021 seeking an accounting of Mrozinski's actions while acting as his father's power of attorney.An estate case was also opened in Indiana, while separate proceedings were initiated in California to handle property located there.The dispute later expanded to include TransAmerican, Inc., a corporation owned by their father and managed by Mrozinski. Clark filed another action in 2023 seeking access to the company's corporate records. That case was subsequently consolidated with the existing proceedings.After several years of litigation, the siblings participated in mediation on July 9, 2024, and signed a settlement agreement. Under its terms, the estate was to transfer certain California real estate to Clark, while he agreed to purchase certain Indiana real estate from the estate.Disagreements emerged soon after the agreement was signed. Both siblings accused the other of failing to fulfil their obligations. In August 2024, they filed separate motions asking the court to enforce the settlement, with Clark alternatively requesting that it be terminated.On September 16, 2024, the trial court rejected Clark's request and directed both parties to proceed in good faith under the agreement. It clarified that disputes concerning the California property would be decided by the California court, while it retained authority over the remaining claims. Clark subsequently filed objections in the California estate proceedings, challenging aspects of the settlement and arguing that it was unenforceable.Mrozinski later asked the Indiana court to hold Clark in contempt, arguing that his objections in California violated the September 2024 order and the settlement agreement. The California court rejected his objections in May 2025.In October 2025, the Indiana trial court found that Clark had knowingly and willingly violated its earlier order. It determined that his failure to comply had caused Mrozinski and the entities she represented to incur $117,655.50 in additional taxes, insurance and security expenses. The court also included $51,617.75 in attorney fees and another $8,579.61 in expenses, bringing the total to $177,852.86. After Clark filed a motion to correct error, the court amended its order in January 2026 but left the sanctions in place.Clark challenged the decision on appeal, arguing that he had not acted in bad faith and had not received sufficient notice that damages would be considered at the hearing. The appeals court rejected his arguments concerning the sanctions hearing. It found that the earlier order clearly required him to comply with the settlement and that he had sufficient notice that financial damages and attorney fees were being sought.The court also noted that Clark had not presented a sufficiently developed argument challenging the amount or type of sanctions.On November 13, 2026, the Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed the sanctions of $177,852.86 against Clark. It also remanded the case for the trial court to consider whether Mrozinski could recover additional attorney fees incurred during the appeal. The appeals judges declined to award appellate attorney fees themselves, finding that Clark's procedural errors did not meet the required standard for such an award.The decision leaves the original sanctions intact while allowing the lower court to consider further legal costs. Article Title: Los Angeles City Council adopts Diwali resolution, honours Indian Consul General
Article Text:
Los Angeles celebrates Diwali with resolution recognising Indian-American community

Indian Consul General honoured for strengthening ties

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Indian cultural performances mark Diwali celebrations

The Los Angeles City Council unanimously adopted a resolution recognising Diwali and honoured India's Consul General to Los Angeles, Dr KJ Srinivasa, during a celebration of the festival at the city's iconic City Hall on Friday.The event was hosted by Los Angeles Mayor-elect and City Councilmember Nithya Raman and attended by Srinivasa, members of the City Council, distinguished guests and representatives of the Indian-American community.The resolution extended Diwali greetings to people across Los Angeles and recognised the contributions of South Asian communities to the city. It highlighted the festival's message of the victory of light over darkness and knowledge over ignorance, along with its values of kindness, generosity, compassion, unity, gratitude and goodwill.It also acknowledged Diwali as a celebration that transcends religious boundaries and brings communities together in a spirit of peace, prosperity and happiness.A key highlight of the event was the presentation of a Certificate of Recognition to Srinivasa by Raman on behalf of the city. The honour recognised his leadership as the inaugural Consul General of India in Los Angeles and his engagement with communities across Southern California, Arizona, New Mexico and Nevada.The citation also acknowledged his efforts to strengthen links between Los Angeles and India in trade, technology and culture. It highlighted his contribution as the city prepares to host the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games (LA28), noting his role in building connections and bringing communities together.In his address, Srinivasa congratulated Raman on her election and extended his best wishes for her forthcoming tenure. Recalling his first welcome at City Hall during the Diwali celebrations in 2025, shortly after he assumed office, he thanked her and the City Council for their continued support and encouragement for the Indian-American community.The Consul General also reaffirmed his commitment to working with the incoming Los Angeles administration to expand cooperation in trade, investment, technology, innovation, education, creative industries and cultural exchanges.He said both sides would explore fresh opportunities for collaboration ahead of LA28. Srinivasa also highlighted the Indian-American diaspora's role in strengthening economic partnerships, cultural understanding and people-to-people ties between India and the US.The event featured performances showcasing India's cultural traditions, including Carnatic music, tabla, Indian classical dance and Bhangra. City Councilmembers, including John Lee, joined hundreds of representatives from Indian-American community organisations at the celebration.Raman welcomed Srinivasa back to City Hall and reiterated their shared commitment to strengthening relations between India and Los Angeles.The Consulate General said the celebration reflected the Indian-American community's growing contributions to the city's civic, economic and cultural life. It also highlighted the importance of India-Los Angeles engagement within the broader India-US partnership, with cultural exchanges serving as a means of building closer ties between the two countries.
Article Summary: The Los Angeles City Council unanimously adopted a resolution recognising Diwali and honoured India's Consul General to Los Angeles, Dr KJ Srinivasa. The event was hosted by Los Angeles Mayor-elect and City Councilmember Nithya Raman.

Article Title: A New York woman won $2 million for pain and suffering after a car crash and spinal fusion surgery; on November 12, an appeals court ordered a new damages trial unless she accepts $1.35 million instea
Article Text:
Representative Image (AI-generated)

Woman underwent cervical spinal fusion surgery after accident

Appeals court rejects challenge to expert testimony

$2 million award reduced to $1.35 million

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A serious car accident can leave injuries that require major surgery and have lasting effects on a person's life. In New York, a woman who underwent spinal fusion surgery after a collision was initially awarded $2 million for past pain and suffering by a jury. However, the New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department, has ruled that the amount was higher than what could be considered reasonable compensation and ordered a reduction or a new trial on damages.In a November 12, 2026 decision available on Justia, the appeals court modified the earlier ruling in Estela Larrea v. Sanitation Salvage Corp. et al. The judges vacated the $2 million award and gave Larrea 30 days after entry of the order to accept $1.35 million instead. If she does not agree, the case will return to court for a new trial limited to those damages. The appeals court otherwise upheld the lower court's decision.The case concerned Estela Larrea, who was 60 years old when the appeals court considered her compensation. She underwent a C5-C6 anterior cervical discectomy and interbody fusion, a procedure involving the removal of a damaged disc in the neck and the fusion of the affected vertebrae.The surgery involved a titanium plate and a plastic cage incorporating cadaver bone, which was secured with screws. The extent of the procedure formed an important part of the court's assessment of the compensation awarded for her past pain and suffering.A jury had awarded Larrea $2 million for this category of damages. However, Sanitation Salvage Corp. and the other defendants challenged the outcome after the trial, seeking a new trial on damages. They argued that the trial court had improperly prevented their proposed biomechanical engineering expert from testifying. Alternatively, they asked the court to set aside the jury's award and order a new trial on past pain and suffering.The defendants argued that their biomechanical expert should have been permitted to explain the mechanics of the accident and its connection to Larrea's injuries. The trial court had conducted a hearing under the Frye standard, which examines whether a scientific methodology is generally accepted in the relevant field. The First Department upheld the exclusion of the proposed expert. It found that the defendants had failed to establish that his personal injury-causation analysis was generally accepted in biomechanics.The judges also identified problems with the information used by the expert. He had relied on assumptions about the weights of the two vehicles that were not supported by the evidence. He was also unaware that the truck involved in the collision carried a large metal construction container and did not know its weight.Other details were missing from his analysis. The expert did not know Larrea's body position at the time of impact or the type of seatbelt and headrest fitted in her vehicle. He was also unaware of her testimony that her car had moved approximately nine feet forward despite her foot being on the brake.The court further noted that the expert had not known that tape visible in photographs of Larrea's vehicle had been placed there after the accident. The tape obstructed part of the damage shown in the photographs. The appeals judges concluded that the expert's opinion lacked sufficient evidentiary value.While the appeals court upheld the exclusion of the defence expert, it separately examined whether the jury's compensation was reasonable. It concluded that the $2 million award for past pain and suffering materially exceeded what would be considered reasonable compensation under New York law.In reaching that conclusion, the judges referred to earlier cases involving spinal injuries and fusion procedures. These included a 2019 decision in which $1 million was considered reasonable compensation for a 69-year-old plaintiff, as well as earlier cases involving spinal fusion surgery and awards of $900,000 and $400,000. The court therefore vacated the $2 million award and ordered a new trial on past pain and suffering unless Larrea agrees to accept $1.35 million within 30 days after entry of the order.If she does not, a new trial will take place on that part of the damages.The November 12 ruling does not overturn the jury's entire verdict or allow the defendants' biomechanical expert to testify. Instead, it addresses the specific amount awarded for past pain and suffering while leaving the other aspects of the lower court's decision intact.
Article Summary: Estela Larrea underwent cervical spinal fusion surgery after a collision. She was initially awarded $2 million for past pain and suffering by a jury. However, the New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department, has ruled that the amount was higher than what could be considered reasonable compensation.

Article Title: NFL star Fred Warner and wife Sydney support pregnant women and single mothers through a San Jose charity, hosting a dinner and donating essential supplies to families in crisis
Article Text:
Fred and Sydney Warner host dinner for single mothers and donate essentials

Both raised by single mothers, Fred and Sydney Warner share a message of support

What CityTeam’s Heritage Home provides

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

During the NFL season, much of Fred Warner’s time is taken up by training, matches and commitments with the San Francisco 49ers. But away from the field, the linebacker and his wife, Sydney, have also been making time for a cause rooted in their own family experiences. The couple recently brought together single mothers and their children for an evening in the Bay Area, combining a shared meal with donations of everyday essentials. The gathering was organised in partnership with a San Jose organisation that provides residential support to pregnant women and new mothers dealing with difficult circumstances.According to the San Francisco 49ers, the gathering, hosted by Fred and Sydney Warner, was held in collaboration with CityTeam’s Heritage Home programme. Mothers and children sat down for a meal in an outdoor setting, while supplies donated for the families were made available nearby.The contributions included blankets, nappies, toys and other household essentials. The evening also gave the couple an opportunity to spend time with the women receiving support, rather than simply make a donation through an organisation.The Instagram post shared on social media showed the Warners, accompanied by their young daughter Bella, interacting with guests.The couple were seen greeting and embracing some of the mothers before joining them for dinner.For Fred and Sydney, supporting single mothers was connected to their own upbringing. Both were raised by single mothers, an experience Sydney discussed in an Instagram post documenting the event.She spoke about how their mothers managed the difficulties of raising children while dealing with personal challenges of their own. Their experiences, she suggested, had influenced the way both she and Fred approached family life and their understanding of the pressures faced by women raising children without a partner.The couple also used the gathering to speak directly to the mothers. Sydney told the women that the circumstances they were currently facing did not have to determine what lay ahead for them or their children.Fred, meanwhile, thanked the guests for allowing the couple to be part of the evening. He said they were grateful to be in a position to offer assistance and wanted to support the families in whatever way they could.The event was organised alongside CityTeam, a non-profit organisation working with people affected by homelessness, poverty, hunger and addiction. Its programmes include residential services for women who need support during pregnancy and after giving birth.Heritage Home, based in San Jose, offers free accommodation and assistance to pregnant women and new mothers experiencing crisis situations. The programme provides a residential setting for women who may be dealing with housing insecurity or other personal difficulties during a particularly demanding period of their lives.By bringing donations and a shared meal to families connected with the programme, the Warners' visit offered practical assistance alongside an opportunity for the women to spend time together.The event also reflected a form of community involvement that has a direct connection to the couple's own family histories. For the mothers who attended, the evening included both donated essentials for their children and an opportunity to meet people who wanted to support them.
Article Summary: Fred and Sydney Warner hosted dinner for single mothers and donated essentials. The event was organised in partnership with CityTeam’s Heritage Home programme.
